meta.title: Operation of Stereo Microscope in Pharmacognosy Laboratory

sections.purpose: To examine the external morphological features, surface texture, trichomes, and gross anatomical structures of crude drugs and plant materials under low magnification with three-dimensional depth perception.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacognosy laboratory for macroscopic evaluation of plant parts, examination of powdered drugs, detection of adulteration, and study of fracture surfaces of crude drugs.
procedure: Place the stereo microscope on a clean, stable, vibration-free surface and ensure the power supply is connected.
Switch on the illumination — select transmitted light (for thin sections, translucent specimens) or reflected/incident light (for opaque surfaces, whole drug material).
Adjust the light intensity using the rheostat/dimmer to provide even, comfortable illumination without glare.
Place the specimen directly on the stage or on a glass plate — for powders, spread a small quantity on a black or white card to contrast with the material.
Select the lowest magnification objective first (typically 7×–10×) to locate the area of interest.
Adjust the interpupillary distance of the eyepieces to match your eyes — the two circles of view should merge into one.
Focus the specimen using the coarse focus knob; refine with the fine focus knob.
Adjust the diopter on each eyepiece individually to correct for differences between your two eyes.
Move the specimen on the stage to explore different areas of the drug material.
Increase magnification (up to 40–45×) for detailed examination of surface features, glands, trichomes, and stomata.
For documentation, attach a camera or smartphone adapter and photograph significant features.
Record observations: colour, odour (smell separately), texture, fracture, surface features, and any adulterant detected.
After use, remove the specimen and clean the stage with a soft brush.
Switch off the illumination and cover the microscope with the dust cover.
Record usage in the equipment logbook.
precautions: Handle the microscope carefully — it is precision optical equipment; never use excessive force on focus knobs.
Clean the objective lenses and eyepieces only with lens paper or a soft lens cleaning cloth — never with regular tissue.
Do not use high illumination intensity for prolonged periods — it reduces lamp life and can heat delicate specimens.
Store the microscope covered to protect from dust when not in use.
Keep chemicals and liquids away from the stage and optical elements.
For sticky or oily specimens, use a clean glass plate on the stage and clean after each use.
Do not disassemble the objectives or eyepieces in the field — send for professional service if required.
